resources.string:
"Two purposes: ① Automatically read the pairing code from the system's \"Wireless debugging\" screen so you don't have to type it by hand (pairing codes expire after two minutes); ② Let the AI assistant read the screen, tap, type, press keys, and take screenshots (screenshots require Android 11+), so it can operate the phone even without ADB or Shizuku.
DeepSeek Harness never records the screen in the background: screen reading only happens the moment the assistant explicitly requests it, and the result goes straight back into the chat — it is never stored on disk or uploaded. The pairing code is only read within two minutes after you tap \"Auto-read pairing code\"."
Can be left empty; you can also set the official or a third-party API and model on the chat page.
After entering the app, checks the selected stable / preview channel in the background; prompts you when a new version is found — you decide whether to download.
Forces the built-in Gecko engine for when the system web page is blank or incompatible; when off, the app picks a working engine automatically. Takes effect after saving and re-entering the chat.
Ask for confirmation before dangerous commands
When on, the AI must ask for consent before running dangerous commands (DSH_CONFIRM); device protection and policy checks always stay active.
Renders the chat page like a desktop browser — good for large screens; usually keep it off on phones. Takes effect after saving and re-entering the chat.
While the local Web is running, serves the chat to devices on the same Wi-Fi via port 3081. Requires the LAN permission — enable only on trusted networks.
Takes effect immediately after switching; the Web page language is switched separately inside the dsh web page.
Shows AI replies and tool-execution status above other apps; needs the overlay permission after saving. Note that bystanders may see the output too.
"Adjust the overlay bar's background color, opacity, line count, font size, and dwell time; you can also choose whether to show the thinking process and original commands."
If the preferred port is taken, a free port is used automatically; see the Launch page for the actual address.
Tries proroot to speed up the container; turn it off if some devices or commands are incompatible, and proot is used instead. Takes effect after saving and restarting the Web.
Collects startup failures, crashes, and recent run output. After downloading, you can find them in Download/DeepSeekHarness.
Add reproduction steps; do not include keys or private chats

"Auto mode keeps IPv6 and only falls back to IPv4 when Node's dual-stack resolution fails. IPv4-compatible mode suits networks that reject AAAA queries, but cannot resolve IPv6-only domains. Takes effect after saving and restarting the Web or opening a new terminal."
Checks the runtime environment, certificates, and plugin status.
Back up and rebuild the environment
Checks all six components and shows each result; missing items are fixed on demand. Checking alone installs nothing, and you can safely stop during a repair.

Tasks keep running after you leave the page; come back to view results. Repairs only touch failed items; a stop request waits for the current operation to finish safely. Backing up stops the Web and fully preserves config, sessions, and local plugins.
First launch requires unpacking the built-in environment. Please wait…
Even without it, app-level APIs like device status and clipboard work; enabling it adds shell commands, simulated taps, and setting changes — needs Developer options → Wireless debugging.
Enable ADB device channel (off by default)
Device commands run via su; keep it off when not rooted.
System sleep freezes background networking; keep-alive only truly works once the app is added to the battery whitelist.
Allow location (needed for LAN / device capabilities)
Device command protection is always active; Root / Shizuku / ADB are each verified independently, and commands are never replayed on another channel when the result is unknown.
Allow sensors (ambient light, acceleration, orientation, etc.)
Safe mode: restore previously enabled third-party plugins
This page does not depend on the Web: you can view recent startup records, restore config snapshots, or uninstall problematic plugins.
Lists only uninstallable third-party plugins; built-in plugins cannot be uninstalled.
Keeps the last three healthy startups and three pre-repair snapshots; saves configuration only — sessions, workspaces, and dependency directories are not copied.
Download error logs · Environment check · Fault repair
Switch npm · Ubuntu packages (APT) · pip mirrors
Use when dsh / npm is corrupted; config and chat history are kept
Gets the latest version from GitHub Releases
Applying an APT source auto-refreshes the index; npm / pip sources take effect immediately.
Or a custom mirror root URL (https://…/ubuntu-ports/)
"Switch between npm / Ubuntu packages (APT) / pip mirror sources. Pick or enter one, then tap \"Apply\" to take effect."
Or a custom pip source URL (https://…/simple)
Type a command, press Enter to run
Fetches the latest release from deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness GitHub Releases and updates automatically via npm inside the container.
Back to the launch page to handle plugins / safe start

One-tap launcher for DeepSeek Harness

Built-in Linux environment — no Termux needed.
Auto-installs and starts, ready out of the box.
Launch, Terminal, Market, Settings — switch in the bottom bar
"Starts the Web UI; tap \"Open\" to launch it inside the app"
Enter the Linux environment and run commands
"The built-in environment unpacks automatically — add your key and you're ready; no key? You can still install first."
"Keep the screen on while unpacking and don't kill the app in the background."
Wait for the environment to unpack
The next page automatically unpacks the built-in Linux environment — nothing to install yourself.
Enter your API key (can be skipped)
Enter it under Settings → Config, or skip it and configure a third-party API in the WebUI later.
Go to the Launch page and start it — ready to use.
Only controls the DeepSeek API key entered in the app; the toggle saves instantly. When off, you must re-enter it after a restore; plugin configs may still contain other credentials.
Back up all data, chats, settings, or plugins on demand.
Backups may contain keys, config, and plugin credentials — keep them safe.
Working directory name inside the runtime environment
Reset and clear actions will ask again; please back up first.
